name: control-home-assistant
description: Carry out home commands through Home Assistant. INPUT (service-neutral, docs/home-control-contract.md): the node before this one returns `commands: [{target, action, value?}]`; `skip: true` does nothing. Actions: turn_on, turn_off, toggle, run (a scene or script), set_temperature (needs `value`). At most 8 commands; the rest are counted as not_run. ALLOW-LIST: the TARGETS config maps each neutral target name to one Home Assistant entity and lists the actions that target allows; set_temperature also needs min and max. A target not in the map, an action it does not allow, or a value outside its bounds is REFUSED and nothing is sent for it — a workflow (or a model) can only do what this node's config names. DRY_RUN DEFAULTS TO TRUE: it reports what it would do and sends nothing until you set DRY_RUN false. OUTPUT: {provider, skipped, dry_run, done, refused, failed, unchanged, not_run, results: [{target, action, status: done|dry_run|refused|failed, reason?, changed?}]}; the results use the neutral names, never an entity id. `done` means Home Assistant ACCEPTED the command, and it accepts one for an entity that does not exist: read `changed` (how many states it says changed) and `unchanged` (done commands that changed nothing). `changed: 0` is a mistyped entity, or a thing already in the state asked for. One command failing is recorded and the rest continue. Written from Home Assistant's documented REST API and not exercised against a live server. BASE_URL must be an https:// address the worker can reach: a home-network address is refused by the worker; use the external address. GRANTS: installs with NO allowed hosts and no secrets: set Home Assistant's external host with update_module_hosts and the token's exact path with update_module_secrets. CREDENTIALS: the module never holds one; AUTH_HEADER carries a vault:// reference the host replaces when the request is sent.

AUTH_HEADER.description: 'Bearer vault://homeassistant/token' — a long-lived access token stored in the vault.

TARGETS.description: Neutral target name -> {entity, allow, min?, max?}. `entity` is the Home Assistant entity id; `allow` lists the actions this target permits; `min` and `max` bound set_temperature. Names: lowercase letters, digits and '_'. At most 64.

DRY_RUN.description: true (the default): report what would be done, send nothing.

setup_instructions.title: Store a token
setup_instructions.detail: Create a long-lived access token in your Home Assistant profile and store it in the vault under homeassistant/token. Tokens are not stored through MCP.

setup_instructions.title: Grant the installed copy
setup_instructions.detail: update_module_hosts with Home Assistant's external host; update_module_secrets with homeassistant/token.

setup_instructions.title: Name the targets
setup_instructions.detail: In the node's TARGETS, give each thing a workflow may act on a neutral name, its entity id and the actions it allows. Leave out anything a workflow should never touch.

setup_instructions.title: Rehearse
setup_instructions.detail: Leave DRY_RUN true and read `results`. Set DRY_RUN false when they are what you expect.
